newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-EXPERIENCE CEDES TO YOUTH IN KOURNIKOVA TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EXPERIENCE CEDES TO YOUTH IN KOURNIKOVA TRIUMPH.

text.p: Youth outgunned experience before an adoring crowd on Tuesday as Wimbledon's newest celebrity Anna Kournikova beat a woman twice her age.

The eye-catching 16-year-old Russian, who was just one year old when Helena Sukova played her first Wimbledon tournament, used fleetness of foot and inch-perfect groundstrokes to outmanoeuvre the tall Czech 2-6 6-2 6-3.
The 1.88 m Sukova, who has reached the quarter-finals here five times, unnerved her young opponent at first with a powerful serve and volley game.
But Kournikova, her long blonde plait flying behind her, got the measure of the serve in the second set and produced returns that whipped past Sukova, licking the lines beyond.

The Florida-based Russian, pupil at the renowned Nick Bolletieri tennis school which nurtured such talents as Monica Seles and Andre Agassi, reached her first match point with one such cross court return.

Sukova saved it but it was not long before another sizzled down the line. The Czech, pushing her serve to its limits in a desperate attempt to counter the young pretender, then sent down a double fault to concede the match.
Kournikova's growing band of admirers, many of them watching court three from the players' balcony, were generous in their applause.
"To reach the quarter-finals is unbelievable," Kournikova said afterwards, though her poise and confidence suggested she was not surprised at all.
"Helena's very experienced and has played a long time on the tour, so I was very happy to win," she added.
Kournikova joins another 16-year-old -- world number one Martina Hingis -- in the quarter-finals and believes their youthful success is born of enthusiasm.
"Maybe we are fresh and maybe we have a great desire to play," she said.
Kournikova meets French Open champion and fourth seed Iva Majoli of Croatia in the quarter-finals.
Majoli, a 19-year-old grass-court specialist, may feel the burden of her three extra years against the speedy Russian, brimming with self-belief.
"We have never played before," Kournikova said. "So it will be interesting."
